name: Hookshot
description: A Native Recompilation Of The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Nintendo Switch 2 Remake
readmeExcerpt:
Hookshot

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator.

Status | How to build | In-game menu | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License

Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows program, the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**.
Discord: https://discord.gg/DVQQJphbBf
> [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy. Everything the build creates (`hookshot.exe`, the generated code, the shader caches and your > saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. ## Project status Experimental. It has only been tested on **one PC** (Ryzen 5 7600X, RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB), mostly in the area at the start of the game. | What | Status | |---|---| | Kokiri Forest: reaching gameplay and walking around | ✅ Works | | Sound, controller, keyboard and saves | ✅ Works | | In-game menu, frame generation and upscaling | ✅ Works | | Black flashes while moving | ✅ Fixed in testing, more play needed | | Performance without frame generation | ⚠️ About 50 fps walking, not yet a steady 60 | | Models with missing pieces (doors, fences, parts of trees) | ✅ Fixed where tested, more play needed | | Stutter when entering new areas | ⚠️ Still happens, mostly the first time | | Ultrawide | ⚠️ The 3D keeps its shape, but the HUD is stretched and the picture is softer | | Hyrule Field and the rest of the game | ❓ Not tested yet | | AMD and Intel cards | ❓ Never tested | ## How to build The game does not come ready-made: it is built on your PC from your copy. **With Hookshot Builder, the easiest:** 1. Download the HookshotBuilder zip from the Releases page, extract it, and run `HookshotBuilder.exe`. Keep the `tools` folder beside it. 2. Choose your game's `.nup`, or your `romfs` and `exefs` folders. The builder checks that it is the right version. 3. Choose a language and a folder for the finished game, and start the build. 4. When it finishes, open `hookshot.exe` in that folder. **From the command line:** ```powershell python -I nx2/make_game.py --nup "C:\path\your-game.nup" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US ``` Or with folders: ```powershell python -I nx2/make_game.py --romfs "C:\path\romfs" --exefs "C:\path\exefs" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US ``` Add `--check` with your `.nup` or `--exefs` to only check the game's version. It builds nothing. A build takes about 40 minutes, and you can use your PC in the meantime. ### On Linux 1. Download `Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage` from the Releases page (or the Linux AppImage workflow's artifact), make it executable (`chmod +x`) and start it. It is Hookshot Builder with everything it needs inside: the compiler, the libraries and the Vulkan renderer. Nothing else has to be installed. 2. Choose your `.nup` (or your `romfs` and `exefs` folders), a language and a folder for the game, and build. 3. When it finishes, press Play. The game is also added to your applications menu. The same AppImage starts that game without opening the builder: `./Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage --play`, or `--play ~/Games/Hookshot` for a different folder. The game itself is `hookshot` in the folder you chose: it runs without the AppImage. From the command line: `./Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage --cli --nup ~/your-game.nup --out ~/Games/Hookshot` (the same options as `make_game.py`). You need a 64-bit x86 PC with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora, Arch, SteamOS ...), a Vulkan 1.3 driver with mesh shaders (Mesa or NVIDIA), and the same memory and disk space as on Windows. The build's own files go to `~/.cache/hookshot-builder`. Saves go in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/hookshot` (`~/.local/share/hookshot`). A `user` folder beside the game from an earlier build is moved there once. To choose how many files compile at once, launch the builder from a terminal with, for example, `HOOKSHOT_JOBS=2 ./Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage` (replace the filename with the one you downloaded). Or run `export HOOKSHOT_JOBS=2` and launch the AppImage from that same terminal. Use a positive whole number; `0`, an empty value or leaving it unset keeps automatic selection. The Linux builder's automatic selection still uses `RX_JOBS` when set, otherwise its existing memory limit. The `--cli` route also accepts `--jobs 2`. These are build settings: `hookshot_env.txt` is read by the running game, not by the builder. Switches to test (`RX_VK_NOOPT=1` and the others) go in `hookshot_env.txt` beside the game, one `NAME=VALUE` a line, as on Windows. `RX_VK_MOVIE_UPSCALE=linear` replaces the movie's neural upscale with the existing linear path. The default `auto` behavior keeps the networks and falls back only when movie GPU time exceeds the existing 40 ms trigger. This switch does not change the gameplay upscaler and can make movie images look softer. It works on Windows and Linux; `RX_VK_NETWORK_KEEP=all` takes precedence and keeps the movie networks enabled. Building it yourself without the AppImage: `clang` and `lld` (LLVM 23 or newer reads the play profile; an older one builds without it), Python 3 with `lz4`, `numpy`, `capstone`, `unicorn` and `zstandard`, FFmpeg's development files (with dav1d, for the movies) and SDL2. Then `python -I nx2/make_game.py ...` as above, with `RX_CPM` pointing at a folder with Vulkan-Headers, SPIRV-Headers and VulkanMemoryAllocator in CPM's layout (`scripts/linux/deps.sh` makes one). `scripts/linux/deps.sh` and `scripts/linux/appimage.sh` make the AppImage. ### Updating to a newer release A new release is not a patch to your game folder: the game is built again from your copy, with the new code. Your saves and settings are kept. What changed in each release is in [changelog.txt](changelog.txt). 1. Close the game. 2. To be safe, copy your saves somewhere first: the `user` folder beside `hookshot.exe` on Windows, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux. 3. Get the new release: - **Hookshot Builder:** download the new HookshotBuilder zip and extract it to a new folder (with its `tools` folder). The old builder folder can then be deleted. - **Linux:** download the new AppImage and make it executable. The old one can be deleted, the game is not removed with it. - **Command line:** `git pull` in your clone, and take the `tools` folder's contents (see [What you need](#what-you-need)) from the new HookshotBuilder zip, as they can change between releases. 4. Build again with the same `.nup` (or `romfs` and `exefs` folders) and **the same game folder** as before. With the same `.nup`, the game is not read again, but the translation and the compile still run, so it takes about as long as the first build. 5. Start the game as before. What a new build keeps and what it replaces in the game folder: | Kept | Replaced | |---|---| | Your saves (`user`, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux) | `hookshot.exe` (`hookshot` on Linux) and its files | | `hookshot_options.ini`, the in-game menu's choices | `image.bin` and the shader list | | `hookshot_env.txt` | `language.txt`, written again with the language you choose | ### What you need - Nothing to install for the build itself: Hookshot Builder brings its own compiler ([llvm-mingw](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw), as TotK Recomp does), Python and libraries. Visual Studio and the Windows SDK are no longer needed. - 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. - A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver. Only NVIDIA has been tested. - 16 GB of RAM or more. A run uses about 10 GB. - About 60 GB free while building. - **Your copy of the game at the supported version:** program `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072, build `e0f3ccfa`. Other versions do not work. To build from the command line you also need: - Python 3 with `lz4`, `numpy`, `capstone`, `unicorn` and `zstandard`: `pip install lz4 numpy capstone "unicorn>=2.1,<2.2" zstandard` Use Python from python.org: the Microsoft Store's Python installs packages where `python -I` does not look. - [llvm-mingw](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw) (the `ucrt-x86_64` build), with `HOOKSHOT_MINGW` set to its folder. Without it the build uses the clang from [emsdk](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk) at `C:\emsdk` with Visual Studio's C++ tools and the Windows SDK (`HOOKSHOT_MSVC=1` forces that route). - Visual Studio 2022 with .NET 8, only if you want to change the builder itself. - The prebuilt tools that go in `third_party/`: `a64emit`, `lld-link`, `zbic` and SDL2. - What the HookshotBuilder zip carries in its `tools` folder and a clone does not. The builder sets the variables below itself; from the command line, set them before you run `make_game.py`: - `tools\cpm`: the Vulkan headers and FFmpeg. Set `RX_CPM` to this folder. Without it the build leaves out `hookshot_vk.dll`, the Vulkan renderer, and says nothing. - `tools\wgpu-native`: set `WGPU_NATIVE` to this folder. - `tools\third_party\sdl2\SDL2.dll`: copy it to `third_party\sdl2\`. - `tools\work`: copy it, with its `image` folder, to `work\`. It holds the hot-function list, the link order, the profile and the icon; without them the game builds but runs slower. ### What this does on your PC - The build reads your game and never changes it. readmeHtml:
Hookshot

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator.

Status | How to build | In-game menu | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License

Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows program, the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game.

Discord: https://discord.gg/DVQQJphbBf

Important

This repository does not contain the game, keys or an executable, and it does not explain how to get them. You need your own copy. Everything the build creates (hookshot.exe, the generated code, the shader caches and your saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files.

Project status

Experimental. It has only been tested on one PC (Ryzen 5 7600X, RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB), mostly in the area at the start of the game.

What Status
Kokiri Forest: reaching gameplay and walking around ✅ Works
Sound, controller, keyboard and saves ✅ Works
In-game menu, frame generation and upscaling ✅ Works
Black flashes while moving ✅ Fixed in testing, more play needed
Performance without frame generation ⚠️ About 50 fps walking, not yet a steady 60
Models with missing pieces (doors, fences, parts of trees) ✅ Fixed where tested, more play needed
Stutter when entering new areas ⚠️ Still happens, mostly the first time
Ultrawide ⚠️ The 3D keeps its shape, but the HUD is stretched and the picture is softer
Hyrule Field and the rest of the game ❓ Not tested yet
AMD and Intel cards ❓ Never tested

How to build

The game does not come ready-made: it is built on your PC from your copy.

With Hookshot Builder, the easiest:

  1. Download the HookshotBuilder zip from the Releases page, extract it, and run HookshotBuilder.exe. Keep the tools folder beside it.
  2. Choose your game's .nup, or your romfs and exefs folders. The builder checks that it is the right version.
  3. Choose a language and a folder for the finished game, and start the build.
  4. When it finishes, open hookshot.exe in that folder.

From the command line:

python -I nx2/make_game.py --nup "C:\path\your-game.nup" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US

Or with folders:

python -I nx2/make_game.py --romfs "C:\path\romfs" --exefs "C:\path\exefs" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US

Add --check with your .nup or --exefs to only check the game's version. It builds nothing.

A build takes about 40 minutes, and you can use your PC in the meantime.

On Linux

  1. Download Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage from the Releases page (or the Linux AppImage workflow's artifact), make it executable (chmod +x) and start it. It is Hookshot Builder with everything it needs inside: the compiler, the libraries and the Vulkan renderer. Nothing else has to be installed.
  2. Choose your .nup (or your romfs and exefs folders), a language and a folder for the game, and build.
  3. When it finishes, press Play. The game is also added to your applications menu. The same AppImage starts that game without opening the builder: ./Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage --play, or --play ~/Games/Hookshot for a different folder. The game itself is hookshot in the folder you chose: it runs without the AppImage.

From the command line: ./Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage --cli --nup ~/your-game.nup --out ~/Games/Hookshot (the same options as make_game.py).

You need a 64-bit x86 PC with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora, Arch, SteamOS ...), a Vulkan 1.3 driver with mesh shaders (Mesa or NVIDIA), and the same memory and disk space as on Windows. The build's own files go to ~/.cache/hookshot-builder. Saves go in $XDG_DATA_HOME/hookshot (~/.local/share/hookshot). A user folder beside the game from an earlier build is moved there once.

To choose how many files compile at once, launch the builder from a terminal with, for example, HOOKSHOT_JOBS=2 ./Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage (replace the filename with the one you downloaded). Or run export HOOKSHOT_JOBS=2 and launch the AppImage from that same terminal. Use a positive whole number; 0, an empty value or leaving it unset keeps automatic selection. The Linux builder's automatic selection still uses RX_JOBS when set, otherwise its existing memory limit. The --cli route also accepts --jobs 2. These are build settings: hookshot_env.txt is read by the running game, not by the builder. Switches to test (RX_VK_NOOPT=1 and the others) go in hookshot_env.txt beside the game, one NAME=VALUE a line, as on Windows.

RX_VK_MOVIE_UPSCALE=linear replaces the movie's neural upscale with the existing linear path. The default auto behavior keeps the networks and falls back only when movie GPU time exceeds the existing 40 ms trigger. This switch does not change the gameplay upscaler and can make movie images look softer. It works on Windows and Linux; RX_VK_NETWORK_KEEP=all takes precedence and keeps the movie networks enabled.

Building it yourself without the AppImage: clang and lld (LLVM 23 or newer reads the play profile; an older one builds without it), Python 3 with lz4, numpy, capstone, unicorn and zstandard, FFmpeg's development files (with dav1d, for the movies) and SDL2. Then python -I nx2/make_game.py ... as above, with RX_CPM pointing at a folder with Vulkan-Headers, SPIRV-Headers and VulkanMemoryAllocator in CPM's layout (scripts/linux/deps.sh makes one). scripts/linux/deps.sh and scripts/linux/appimage.sh make the AppImage.

Updating to a newer release

A new release is not a patch to your game folder: the game is built again from your copy, with the new code. Your saves and settings are kept. What changed in each release is in changelog.txt.

  1. Close the game.
  2. To be safe, copy your saves somewhere first: the user folder beside hookshot.exe on Windows, or ~/.local/share/hookshot on Linux.
  3. Get the new release:
    • Hookshot Builder: download the new HookshotBuilder zip and extract it to a new folder (with its tools folder). The old builder folder can then be deleted.
    • Linux: download the new AppImage and make it executable. The old one can be deleted, the game is not removed with it.
    • Command line: git pull in your clone, and take the tools folder's contents (see What you need) from the new HookshotBuilder zip, as they can change between releases.
  4. Build again with the same .nup (or romfs and exefs folders) and the same game folder as before. With the same .nup, the game is not read again, but the translation and the compile still run, so it takes about as long as the first build.
  5. Start the game as before.

What a new build keeps and what it replaces in the game folder:

Kept Replaced
Your saves (user, or ~/.local/share/hookshot on Linux) hookshot.exe (hookshot on Linux) and its files
hookshot_options.ini, the in-game menu's choices image.bin and the shader list
hookshot_env.txt language.txt, written again with the language you choose

What you need

  • Nothing to install for the build itself: Hookshot Builder brings its own compiler (llvm-mingw, as TotK Recomp does), Python and libraries. Visual Studio and the Windows SDK are no longer needed.
  • 64-bit Windows 10 or 11.
  • A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver. Only NVIDIA has been tested.
  • 16 GB of RAM or more. A run uses about 10 GB.
  • About 60 GB free while building.
  • Your copy of the game at the supported version: program 0400486024DEC000, update v131072, build e0f3ccfa. Other versions do not work.

To build from the command line you also need:

  • Python 3 with lz4, numpy, capstone, unicorn and zstandard: pip install lz4 numpy capstone "unicorn>=2.1,<2.2" zstandard Use Python from python.org: the Microsoft Store's Python installs packages where python -I does not look.
  • llvm-mingw (the ucrt-x86_64 build), with HOOKSHOT_MINGW set to its folder. Without it the build uses the clang from emsdk at C:\emsdk with Visual Studio's C++ tools and the Windows SDK (HOOKSHOT_MSVC=1 forces that route).
  • Visual Studio 2022 with .NET 8, only if you want to change the builder itself.
  • The prebuilt tools that go in third_party/: a64emit, lld-link, zbic and SDL2.
  • What the HookshotBuilder zip carries in its tools folder and a clone does not. The builder sets the variables below itself; from the command line, set them before you run make_game.py:
    • tools\cpm: the Vulkan headers and FFmpeg. Set RX_CPM to this folder. Without it the build leaves out hookshot_vk.dll, the Vulkan renderer, and says nothing.
    • tools\wgpu-native: set WGPU_NATIVE to this folder.
    • tools\third_party\sdl2\SDL2.dll: copy it to third_party\sdl2\.
    • tools\work: copy it, with its image folder, to work\. It holds the hot-function list, the link order, the profile and the icon; without them the game builds but runs slower.

What this does on your PC

  • The build reads your game and never changes it. It writes to the folder you choose and to %LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder.
  • The romfs is hard-linked instead of copied where the disk allows it.
  • To uninstall, delete the game folder and %LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder.

If something goes wrong

Problem What to do
"Hookshot supports build e0f3ccfa" Check that you chose the right game with its update installed
The game opens and closes Update your graphics driver
Stutter the first time you see something Normal for now: shaders are being prepared. It gets better when you pass through the same place again
The game is in the wrong language Change the code in language.txt beside the game. The file lists them all

If the problem continues, report it with where you were in the game, your graphics card and a screenshot or video. Never send game files.

In-game menu

Press Insert in game, or on a controller the Home button (or Select and Start together). Everything is off by default, and your choices are saved in hookshot_options.ini beside the game. On a controller the D-pad chooses and changes, the bottom face button changes too, and the right one closes the menu.

Option Choices
Quality preset Custom, Minimum (4GB), Low (6GB), Balanced (8GB), High (12GB), Ultra (16GB+)
Frame generation Off, 2x, 3x, 4x
Frame pacing Off, On
Resolution Auto (the game's own dynamic resolution), 100%, 75%, 67%, 50%
Upscaling Off, Catmull-Rom, Lanczos
Sharpness 0 to 100%
Game speed Per frame, Real time
Handheld profile Off, On
Ultrawide 16:9, Monitor's shape
FPS counter Off, On

With Game speed on Per frame, the game runs slower whenever it is below 60 fps. Real time keeps it at normal speed. Upscaling and Sharpness also work when Frame generation is Off.

Controls

Use a controller, or the keyboard and mouse. On the keyboard, W A S D move and the arrow keys turn the camera.

To change which gamepad button or key presses a Switch button, open the in-game menu's Controls page. Choose a button and a column, press Enter (or the bottom face button), then the new button or key; Delete clears it, and Reset to defaults puts them all back. A gamepad button taken from another Switch button swaps with it. The page saves them in hookshot_options.ini, where you can also write them yourself:

pad_a=0
key_a=69,13

pad_<button> is a gamepad input by position: 0 bottom face button, 1 right, 2 left, 3 top, 4 Select or Back, 5 Home, 6 Start, 7 and 8 the stick presses, 9 and 10 the shoulder buttons, 11 to 14 the D-pad (up, down, left, right), 15 and 16 the triggers, -1 none. key_<button> is one or two Windows key codes in decimal (69 is E, 13 Enter), 0 none. The buttons are a b x y l r zl zr plus minus ls rs left up right down. A button the file leaves out keeps its default.

Mods

Put mods in a mods folder beside hookshot.exe (or point HOS_MODS at another folder), in the layout emulators use: mods/<name>/romfs/... holds files that replace or add to the game's own. Deeper layouts such as mods/contents/<title id>/<name>/romfs work too. A folder whose name starts with - or _ is off. When two mods have the same file, the one whose folder name sorts last wins, so name them 01-..., 02-... to set the order.

Only RomFS mods are loaded. exefs patches (.pchtxt, .ips) are left out: Hookshot compiles the game's code ahead of time, so patching its instructions would need a rebuild. The log (hookshot_log.txt when started from its icon) names each mod and the files read from it.

How it works

  1. nx2/lift.py translates the game's ARM64 code to C.
  2. nx2/build.py compiles that C together with host/, which plays the part of the console's system.
  3. host/nvn_native.c records the game's NVN2 graphics calls, and gpu/vk/ replays them on Vulkan.
  4. Switch 2 Ampere shaders are lowered to Maxwell (lower_to_maxwell.h) and translated to SPIR-V by Eden's shader recompiler.

More detail is in the development guide and the design notes.

Want to help?

Testing on other graphics cards and reporting the result already helps a lot, and so does playing further into the game than anyone has yet.

Bigger ways to help:

  • Linux testing. The Linux build (host/posix) has been tested on one PC so far: reports from other distributions and graphics cards help.
  • Fixes in your own fork. Fork the project, fix what you find and send the change back. Keep game files, keys and anything generated from your game out of it.

CONTRIBUTING.md has the setup, the test commands, the code conventions and what a good pull request looks like.

Credits

Hookshot exists thanks to the work of many people:

  • NotRexed: Hookshot, BlueShell (Mario Kart World), Skybound (Tears of the Kingdom) and the a64-kit tools.
  • Eden and Eglantine: the shader recompiler and Switch 2 shader work.
  • suyu: the graphics decoders and the AArch64 translator.
  • seedds/nxnative: reference for how task and mesh shaders work.
  • EvilBoyce / evilmfkr (EvilOOT): the GPU culling that brings back Kokiri's foliage (trees, ferns, grass, falling leaves, fireflies), the ambient light probes, the pond's water, the game's own fog, the freeze after Load (Horizon's mutex handoff) and the exposure flicker fix.
  • zortos293/Lichii: reference for Ampere shader lowering, and its compare-exchange retry fix.
  • mstorsjo/llvm-mingw: the bundled Windows compiler (no Visual Studio needed).
  • kinnay/zbic, Opus and SDL: decompression, audio and controllers.
  • sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp: this README's layout, and its notes confirmed the mesh stage's control section.
  • MythosOfs/Orchid: the fog and exposure workaround for Ocarina of Time.
  • Mesa (NAK): the reference for Ampere's instruction encoding.
  • Everyone who sent fixes: SkippySteve (Linux and the AppImage, and many more), klimovich008, d3zessete, chrispository, vzeol, monsterlag, leonidasmark, Segmentree, Zorkats, ShyVortex, hiKareeem, gab9281 and i900gaming, among others.

License

Hookshot is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later). It includes code from Eden, suyu and Orchid, which are under the GPL too. Third-party parts under other licenses that work with the GPL (Sirit, the Vulkan Memory Allocator, SDL, Opus, stb, zbic and the a64-kit tools) keep their own notices in their folders.

Hookshot is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. The Legend of Zelda and Ocarina of Time are trademarks of Nintendo.

releases.name: Ultrawide, AMD black-screen fix, fewer shader stalls, less flicker
releases.body:
**Download `HookshotBuilder.exe`** and run it (an installed builder updates itself: the game offers the update at start, a ~4 MB download and only the changed files compiled).

## Ultrawide, for real
With **Ultrawide** on in the Insert menu (or a window wider than 16:9), the game now draws a wider picture instead of stretching a 16:9 one: you see more of the world at the sides, with the HUD, menus and movies kept in the middle 16:9. Tested at 21:9 (3440x1440) and 32:9, including the pause menu. Based on the ultrawide patch sites NX2navi uses, credited to Ivan0xFF (MIT).

## Black screen after the opening (AMD) and long shader waits
- **Compute shaders compile in the background.** On AMD cards a single compute shader took the driver 15–23 seconds, and the game froze with a black screen while it did. Now the game keeps going and that effect appears once it's ready.
- **Twice as many shaders are prepared before the first start** (PR #474: the game's compute and effect shaders were missing from the list), so far fewer compile while you play. The first start's preparation takes longer (about 2½ minutes on a 12-thread PC).

releases.name: No Visual Studio needed, fewer flashes, controls, faster
releases.body:
**Build again with this Hookshot Builder** (Windows: `HookshotBuilder.zip`; Linux: the `.AppImage` below, added by the build a few minutes after this release). Your saves and settings stay where they are.

## No more Visual Studio or Windows SDK
The builder now brings its own compiler (llvm-mingw, as the TotK port does). You no longer need Visual Studio, the Build Tools or the Windows SDK: unzip, pick your game files, build. "Windows SDK not found" is gone.

## Fixes
- **Flicker and white flashes**: CPU reads of GPU results now wait for the work that writes them (EvilBoyce's fix, #296), and the VRAM mirrors no longer overwrite the GPU query results that decide which passes run (fewer one-frame dark frames).
- **Missing geometry on every GPU**: 30 mesh shaders that failed to translate (`LoadGlobalS16`, #351) now work.
- **CPUs without AVX2** (older Xeons, Ivy Bridge): the game is built for your CPU and no longer crashes at start (#363).
- **User folders with accents** (e.g. `Magalhães`) no longer break the build (#230).
- **Movie thread crash** when memory runs short (#342).
- **Black movies on Windows**: if Windows has no AV1 decoder, the game now tells you and opens the free "AV1

releases.name: New installer: one small download, small updates, foliage and AMD fixes
releases.body:
## A new installer: one small download

**Download `HookshotBuilder.exe`** (170 KB) and run it. That's the only file you need: it downloads the builder and its tools (about 460 MB, once), checks every part against its checksum, and opens the new Hookshot window.

If you have an older Hookshot Builder, its update button will ask you to download the new version yourself this one time; after that, updates are automatic and small.

- **Finds your game files by itself**: .nup files in Downloads, Desktop, Documents and the top of each drive, each with its version checked. Browse or drag and drop still work.
- **Game files › Build › Play** in one window, with the time left, Play, and Desktop and Start menu shortcuts at the end.
- **Small updates**: the game's update offer now downloads only what changed (about 4 MB when only Hookshot's code changed), and only changed files are compiled again. A test update took 3 minutes instead of 39, and your current game stays playable until the new one is complete.

releases.body:
**Download `HookshotBuilder.exe`** and run it, or accept the game's update offer (a ~4 MB download, a few minutes of compiling).

## Setup and builder
- **"Github answered with an error"** (#537, #538, #539, #543, #544): GitHub's release download links failed with 504 for hours.
  HookshotBuilder.exe now tries again (5 times for the list, 4 for each part), and when the release link fails it fetches the same
  file through GitHub's API instead (from PR #546 by nicholasgower).
  *Updated the exe now tries 8 times over ~3 minutes, and a download cut off half way is tried again instead of
  failing at once (#558). The parts already downloaded are kept, so running it again carries on.*
- **Builds stopping at once with `OSError [Errno 22]` or WinError 1224** (#501, #530): a build left running by an earlier one
  (the builder closed, crashed or replaced by an update mid-build) held the work folder's files. A new build now stops that
  leftover build first, and nothing else.
- **Choose the number of build workers** in the Windows builder (PR #517 by monsterlag; #502). Automatic is the default and
  works as before; the Linux builder honours `HOOKSHOT_JOBS` (PR #505).

releases.name: About 45% more fps, texture corruption fix
releases.body:
**Download `HookshotBuilder.exe`** and run it, or accept the game's update offer (a ~3 MB download, a few minutes of compiling).

## About 45% more fps
**PR #523** (hckrman101): every NVN queue shared one fence timeline, so the game's main thread waited on other queues' work at
each submit. Fences are now per queue. On an RTX 4060 Ti in Kokiri Forest: **47 fps, up from 33**, and fewer one-frame flicker
events (43 in ~1,800 frames, 10 of them large; ~55 and 17-24 before).
PR #513's frame wait is in too, on by default on Linux, where its author measured 70 -> 0 flashes (`RX_VK_WAIT_GPU=0` turns it
on anywhere; on Windows here it cost ~10 fps without changing the flicker counts).

## Fixes
- **Texture corruption in long sessions** (#386): a texture the GPU drew is written back into the game's memory before it is
  evicted, so it no longer comes back empty or garbled (dark terrain patches, tiled patterns on the Deku Tree's planks).
- **Crash after a freeze** in combat or when opening the ocarina note sheet (#500): no longer crashes on a texture builder
  the game passes as none.
